title: Using Variational Quantum Algorithm to Solve the LWE Problem
finding: Already maps LWE to BDD and applies QAOA around a classical nearest-plane estimate.
implication: Neither the LWE-to-lattice connection nor a Babai-centered QAOA search is our invention.

title: Quantum-classical hybrid algorithm for solving the learning-with-errors problem on NISQ devices
finding: Reports a small IBM hardware demonstration using a lattice-based hybrid construction for decision-LWE.
implication: Do not claim the first quantum-hardware lattice/LWE experiment; our task and evaluation differ.

title: Heuristic Time Complexity of NISQ Shortest-Vector-Problem Solvers
finding: Studies fixed-angle QAOA and a controlled-mixer variant for SVP; the reported simulations assume ideal devices.
implication: Lattice angle pretraining is established; physical-device behavior is a sensible experimental follow-up.

title: A Practically Scalable Approach to the Closest Vector Problem for Sieving via QAOA with Fixed Angles
finding: Pretrains QAOA angles for constrained CVP on prime lattices arising in sieving. It discusses restricted search-space coverage and structure-dependent conclusions.
implication: Our q-ary toy benchmark is a different instance family, but fixed-angle CVP itself is prior work. Compare with the authors’ public implementation: https://github.com/BenPrie/qaoa-for-cvp.

title: Graph Learning for Parameter Prediction of Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
finding: Uses graph learning to improve QAOA initialization for MaxCut.
implication: Machine learning for QAOA parameters is established. Our modest extension is its evaluation on these lattice instances.

title: Graph Representation Learning for Parameter Transferability in Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
finding: Studies structural representations and donor-instance selection for QAOA parameter transfer.
implication: Even structure-based selection is prior art; describe this project as application and empirical comparison, not a new general algorithm.

title: Transferring linearly fixed QAOA angles: performance and real device results
finding: Demonstrates a compact transferable angle schedule and real-device results for Ising optimization.
implication: Hardware transfer and compact parameter schedules are also established. Normalization and strong fixed-angle controls matter.

title: When the Learning With Errors Problem Meets the Coherent Ising Machine: A Penalty-Free Algorithm-Hardware Co-Design
finding: Proposes a Babai-recentered least-squares QUBO and adaptive encoding for a coherent Ising machine.
implication: Recent related encoding work overlaps our ingredients. Its hardware is different from gate-based IBM QAOA; its claims were not independently reproduced here.

title: IBM Quantum Open Plan
finding: The standard Open Plan allowance is up to ten minutes per rolling 28-day window.
implication: The plan below uses that allowance; it does not depend on promotional access.

title: IBM Quantum workload usage
finding: Usage includes QPU-locked execution and per-sub-job overhead; a quick estimate uses about 0.00035 seconds per execution plus overhead.
implication: Shot counts alone do not guarantee quota compliance. Compile for the chosen device and inspect actual job usage.

title: IBM maximum execution time
finding: Per-job maximum execution time is based on QPU usage. A batch time-to-live is a different limit.
implication: Use per-job caps and a cumulative local usage ledger; retain a reserve.
